reviewer: independent retry_after agent; not P2-6/P2-7 author
verdict: No blocking correctness finding in reviewed product inputs; independent composed runtime probe passed. Final integrated tree still requires its own hash binding and full gates.
composition: Root P2-7 main.cpp with only dispatcher commit one-line BackgroundWorker type adaptation, linked to immutable author P2-6 library; this is an independently composed integration probe, not a final root build claim.

runtime.scope: Independently composed P2-7 HTTP executor plus P2-6 dispatcher, Linux Debug; synthetic loopback RPC only.

static_review: Four fixed lanes with one lease/RPC in flight per lane; read, shared map/crawl and search have independent synchronous callers. Fixture-only setup starts one lane.

Shared startup latch prevents any lease admission until requested threads exist; partial construction requests stop on all initialized lanes before releasing latch and joining. No runtime thread-creation failure injection was performed.

Stop-token-aware condition-variable polling wakes on stop. request_stop visits all lanes before join starts. Destructor and move assignment stop and join old ownership before Store/WebService lifetime ends.

Existing durable lease, token, publication/owner fences and reservation/unknown-budget logic remain in execute/commit paths. Per-category work stays serial; prior global category alternation is no longer a guarantee.
Concrete HTTP worker uses independent per-call connections and IO context. Python worker supports concurrent requests; WorkerPort contract now states the concurrent-call requirement.
Combined HTTP lifetime stops both admission domains before joining, keeps Store/WebService and IO alive while accepted tasks finish, and does not detach execution.
independent_runtime_claims: With first read/map/search RPCs held, all eight default HTTP business workers accept independent synchronous reads; measured peak is eleven physical RPCs.

While all eight HTTP requests stay held, completing each first durable search/read/map permits that category second queued task to start and settle; this verifies progress after saturation rather than merely before saturation.
Each durable category peak remains one; read/map known failure outcomes charge exactly one actual request and zero unknown requests.
An extra queued read cancelled through HTTP before saturation remains cancelled with zero attempts; call counts show no cancelled/failed replay.
Health remains available and business job.get returns 503 E_REQUEST_BACKPRESSURE while saturated. After releasing sync work all accepted calls settle, HTTP admission recovers and process exits zero.
limits: Linux Debug with synthetic loopback Worker; no real external source activation or source audit-state mutation.
Fixture completion was observed under saturation but may have finished before the eight HTTP calls filled; no stronger after-saturation fixture ordering is claimed.
This composed build combines the frozen P2-7 main with one BackgroundWorker type adaptation and author P2-6 core. It is not proof of a later root integrated binary until hashes are bound.
No ASan, TSan, Windows, start-thread failure injection, or arbitrary latency SLA claim from this probe.
Original 64-connection HTTP limit, per-category serialization, and shared storage/JSON contention remain.

preserved_initial_probe_failure.cause: Independent probe SQLite cleanup bug: connection closed inside its transaction context, causing __exit__ to operate on a closed DB. Product is not implicated.
